A.justification: Explicitly covers every requested component — smoke crawl (console errors, failed requests, CWV), interaction tests, visual regression with masking and 0.1% threshold, accessibility (contrast, focus order, ARIA tooltips), blast-radius rules, dark-mode dual-baseline strategy, and exit criteria. Technically sound and clearly staged/gated. Only minor weakness is verbosity and a slight truncation in the final sign-off checklist.

B.justification: Produces solid, runnable Playwright code for smoke and interaction phases with strong blast-radius rules, but truncates during Phase 2 and never delivers visual regression, accessibility, dark-mode baseline, or exit criteria. Partial coverage means it fails several explicit requirements.

C.justification: Highly detailed and technically precise: pinned viewport/DPR config, per-stage pass/fail, mask selectors, 0.1% threshold, and a thorough ARIA role table including tooltip/aria-describedby. Falls short only because the blast-radius section is truncated and the explicit dark-mode baseline strategy and exit criteria sections are absent.

D.justification: Does not deliver a QA plan at all. The response is a meta-question asking whether the user wants a plan extended, referencing a previous answer and a skill checklist. It produces no actual content addressing smoke, interaction, visual regression, accessibility, blast-radius, dark-mode, or exit criteria.

E.justification: Presents a clean six-phase architecture with good code (masking, contrast extraction, pixel-diff) and explicitly names dark-mode baseline and sign-off phases, but truncates before Phase 5/6 and provides no explicit blast-radius rules, dark-mode baseline detail, or exit criteria in the delivered text.

raw_result.pairwise_analysis: A ranks first because it is the only response that fully addresses all seven required sections with dedicated, concrete content (including both the blast-radius rules and the dark-mode dual-baseline strategy that several others omit or truncate). C and E are strong on technical depth and architecture, but both truncate before delivering the dark-mode baseline and exit criteria, with E additionally missing any explicit blast-radius rules. B and D trail because B stops at the interaction phase with no visual/a11y/dark-mode/exit sections, and D fails outright by producing no plan at all — only a clarifying question.
